newsitem.title: USA: Bed tax proposed in Roanoke Rapids, Va.
newsitem.headline: Bed tax proposed in Roanoke Rapids, Va.

text.p: The Roanoke Rapids City Council voted to ask the Virginia Assembly for authority to enact a bed tax to offset potential losses in property tax revenues, the Herald newspaper said Friday.
A tax rate was not set. City officials said a three percent tax would generate $60,000 a year, a four percent tax would bring in $80,000 a year and a five percent tax would raise $100,000 annually.
Guests already pay a nine percent tax on lodging -- six percent levied by the state and a three percent Halifax County occupancy tax.

The city is seeking alternate sources to replace the potential loss of $30,000 a year in property tax revenue after the anticipated closing of a North Carolina Power plant. The city is negotiating to buy the property, which would make it tax-exempt.
The city council and Halifax County commissioners have also agreed to hire a Raleigh consulting firm, LPA Group, to explore the possibility of building a $13 million county airport.
